comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and locks an industrial robot-axis shock absorber through iterative physical test cycles; pr-1307 performs one passive elbow range-of-motion repetition on a training manikin.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key alignment, captive-setscrew loosening, collar rotation, counterholding, relocking, control actuation, and response-based adjustment. pr-1307 requires supporting and articulating a manikin arm to bend the elbow to approximately 90 degrees, then straighten and release it.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable simulated carriage stops within damper travel and energy/velocity limits, without hard-stop contact, excessive rebound, overload, setting drift, unsafe energized adjustment, or prohibited state writes. pr-1307 requires bending the elbow to a right angle, returning the arm to the bed, and letting go; its record provides no numeric safety, force, damage, or hold thresholds.
comparison.reason: The tasks test meaningfully different abilities and outcomes: iterative tool-mediated adjustment and retention of a dynamic energy absorber versus direct passive articulation of a patient limb. Their only shared primitives are generic contact and controlled motion, which do not establish overlap.
